name: Levomepromazine
metabolism: On average half of an oral dose reaches the bloodstream as unchanged levomepromazine. It spreads through the body at 23 to 42 L/kg and stays for 15 to 30 hours. A human study after an oral dose found glucuronides, sulfoxide and possibly some unchanged drug in the urine, and unchanged drug in the faeces. At a therapeutic concentration of 10 micromolar, CYP3A4 is the main enzyme doing the 5-sulfoxidation (72%) and the N-demethylation (78%), and CYP1A2 contributes 20% of the 5-sulfoxidation. It leaves slowly, taking about 30 hours, mainly through the urine and faeces; the breakdown products mostly go out in the urine, and on average 10% of the daily dose leaves in the urine as levomepromazine sulfoxide.
summary: Levomepromazine, also known as methotrimeprazine, is a phenothiazine neuroleptic and low-potency antipsychotic. Its analgesic, hypnotic, and antiemetic properties are used mainly in palliative care.
